reviews.text: It's rare to find a sequel that doesn't try too hard to be different. Dungeon Dreams 2 is that rare game. That's not to say that there aren't changes or improvements, because there certainly are. But the best praise I can heap on the game as a sequel is this: I wanted "Dungeon Dreams, but more of it" and that is exactly what I got. And it's awesome. More of what? Everything, really. More quests. More characters. More character customization. More romanceable characters. More minigames. More town customization. More dungeon floors. More loot. Just...more. Don't let an RPGMaker game scare you. It's an RPG made by somebody who loves the RPGs of the past - Suikoden, Azure Dreams, and Persona to name a few - and it shows. There are some bugs and typos here and there, but the dev is active and really good about listening to feedback and actually fixing things. The dev's passion shines through. Are you at least vaguely interested in RPGs that trade broadness for depth? It's well worth a look, especially at the asking price!

I didn't expect much, I'm not into rpgmaker games so thought at best I could use this game to kill a few hours since the art is cute... But I was very wrong, its been days now and I'm still hooked The characters are so precious, I want to spend time with them all... But Lissbeth gets a special spot, she's cute, funny, and doesn't judge me for hanging out near the sewers I have two main gripes with the game as it is which might be improved on with time; 1) Our player character avatar feels very basic compared to most companions. The ginger mage and his drunk archer friend also suffer from the same issue 2) Not being able to dismiss a companion unless you go to your house and use the save book, maybe I'm just dumb and there is a way to do this in a different way that I have not found Finally hear me out, there are some bears on floors 36-39, what if... We as players had the option to enter into a romantic relationship with those bears and have *censored* with them on our first date
A good game and good sequel to DD1, worth the money for the time spent playing.

You are the child of the protagonist in the previous game: Dungeon Dreams, that the developer created several years ago; thankfully, you don't need to play it in order to enjoy this game, but doing so will make it more interesting and fun to see how the characters in the previous game changed within this sequel. In the beginning of the game, you will meet your future ex-girlfriend Reyanna, who you will explain your backstory to that will determine who your parents are; your appearance based on the parent you chose. When selecting a parent, you will get to see a brief pro and cons for being their child. For instance, one character would give bonus attack stats while reducing your luck if chosen as the mom while the pros to choosing a character named Mai would be that she's the canon mom....! Okay... I suppose that this is the game's subtle way of telling me that if I choose any other character as my mom, then whatever I do for the rest of the game is just a big "What IF" story since I didn't choose Mai as my mom as she is the canon choice... Story: The story is very simple, there is a dungeon called the Flux; there is a competition to reach to the very bottom of the dungeon. To get to the dungeon, you would need to enter the Magic Academy's basement; then you can enter the dungeon by going through the hole in the wall which reminds me of Reyanna. I appreciate that there is now a explanation for why characters can only enter as a team up to 4 as the crazy nature of the Flux can separate teams apart if there are more than 4 in a team at any given time. It's fine that the story is a bit simplistic because the meat of the game lies within the... Characters: When meeting an important character with unique art for the very first time, the game will view the character's full art from the bottom before slowly scrolling up to make sure that you will appreciate the art, regardless of whether you wanted to see it or not as the developer paid good money to acquire those art! The writing for the characters and their interactions with each other is an absolute joy to see. Whether it would be characters reacting in certain situations or talking to each other after reaching a specific location or floor. For instance, in the beginning of the game, there is a chance that you will meet your future ex-wife Reyanna at the tavern; if you talk to her, she will plead with you to not tell your BFF Victor that she's drinking at the tavern as he already tried to invite her out numerous times and that she is running out of excuses to politely turn him down. So if you happen to have Victor in your party when you speak with her at that time and location, instead, Victor will get upset that Reyanna never accepted his invitations to go to the Tavern; then Reyanna will do a poor attempt at lying. Other times, certain characters may make choices for you and or lock out certain choices which makes them more alive as a character with their own personality and ideals. What's even better than knowing the characters would be the... Romance: Here we have the juiciest part of the game, once a character's affection for you is high enough and or you are far enough in their personal character quests, you can ask them out. More often then not, you will only have one chance to ask them out; the game is kind enough to warn you that it will be your only chance once it's time to make the choice. I can appreciate being given a choice to enter a romance with a character because in the previous game, *Holds out a hand with palm up horizontally to represent the ground with the second hand vertically on top of it to represent the girl* The moment you recruit and or start the girl's events... *The vertical hand flips onto the horizontal hand* In this sequel, girls won't automatically fall in love with you when you recruit and or start their events except for your overworked and sleep deprived wife Reyanna! So you only have one chance to romance Reyanna the moment you recruit her while all the other girls only chance would occur later in their events. Dating in this game is much easier and less stressful than the prequel. No more will my date ditch me because I'm not a vegetarian like her! Instead, you will have a one time unique dialogue with your date at a dating spot with unique questions and answers to further raise their affection towards you. You can also give them a gift or propose to them when their affection is high enough without having to answer correctly a barrage of random questions. If you want, you can date multiple people at the same time, though be ready to suffer the consequences of some of them permanently leaving your party if they don't like you dating other people. Now to find a girl to romance... Don't worry Reyanna I'll do you later in a new game plus, so how about... This girl! She has a unique art and name so...! Wait, the game won't let me romance her because she's a year or two under 18... Guess I'll just have to romance... Her hot mom instead! So what are the other choices? How about this pretty guard name Odea that you can only recruit as a warrior? What...? I can't romance her because she's so dedicated to working at her job that she makes Reyanna blush!? Alrighty then, how about this cute Ninja that I can only recruit as a thief? What's that? She's a wanted person so I can't marry her either? So who else can I marry!?! Let me cherry pick some examples of who you can marry in this game: Elves, moms, elf who is a mom... If it's not already obvious, I'm just exaggerating it as there are plenty of people you can romance in this game that are not elves or moms. Still funny that there are many elves you can romance in this game as there were no elves you can romance in the prequel. Alright, now that I chosen this teleporting mage named Sally who I can only recruit as a thief as my wife in my first playthrough, time to marry her! Before the wedding start, you can choose where you can marry in this game, though some choices will be locked out depending on who you are marrying due to certain circumstances or your spouse's personal preference. You can then choose who will be your best man or woman which includes your chosen parent and any companions if you fully completed their personal quests, who will then give you a unique gift to celebrate your wedding. Once the wedding venue and best man/woman has been chosen, time to see your chosen spouse will walk towards you to give you a kiss. Afterwards, they will move into your home; contribute some gold which will vary depending on how financially wealthy they are. Since they have lives of their own, they won't always stay at home; will be out to do their job and or hobbies. Karma system: There are many choices you can make within this game that will change the outcome for many characters and events. There are 5 disposition that your character can be depending on your actions: Villain, mean, neutral, honest and Saint. Your disposition can be changed after you go to sleep; the game asks you if you want to be a mean or honest person if you meet the requirements and you can deny the change if you want. It's significantly harder to get the honest and saint disposition due to the scarcity of choices that will make your character lean towards them while there are plenty of mean and villain choices. So... How big of a d*ck will this game let you be...? Um... I would say.... About 6 inches...? I would say more, but I'm reaching the character limit, so in short: Lots of replay-ability, characters to fall in love with and hate and a very good price for the amount of content it provides.

Frankly, this is one of the best made games I've ever played. The depth of content is unbelievable. If you like JRPGs, or mystery dungeon, or dating sims, this is a game you need to play. It has it all. There's only one problem this game has, detailed below. Give me a Mochi romance. I can fix her.

I had some fun with this one, but it's hard for me to just straight up give it a positive review. There are some pros, the leveling system is comprehensive and straight forward, the story is interesting, the gameplay loop is addictive. The cons are simple: triggering events is unknown and just random at many times. Some events tend to trigger but if they trigger before another required event then the game breaks. For example I suddenly got debt to pay. I went and paid the debt off immediately, then suddenly I still can't do business with the merchant guild. I'm soft locked out of major game mechanic which is business development. I went ahead and beat the game.. new game + doesn't really seem worth the trouble once I went through with it.

I waited for this game since I played the first chapter, and I had lots of fun back then. Dungeon Dreams 2 definitely delivers! It is really everything a sequel should be! DD2 has what I loved from the first one, but more. Personally, I really enjoyed each and every side quest. They are really fun, in particular the "special" ones. A couple of them really surprised me! I like the humor, and all the interaction between characters. The tiny little weird things that happen here and there never fail to steal a smile. It shows that the dev took the time to think all this, and had fun doing so. The connections with the first game are a really nice touch! Oh, and you don't need to play the first game to enjoy DD2, but hey... why not play both?!? If you enjoyed the first game, this is for you. If you haven't (yet, lol), and you love games where the environment feels alive and full of character, this game is for you. If you usually play other kinds of games (like I do), shut up, this game is for you.

LIGHTING IN A BOTTLE FOR A SECOND TIME! Okay this developer has proven that the first game really wasnt a fluke, and that here is a talent for created retro JRPGs that you don't often see. Its got its flaws, sure, but overall, its an excellent follow up to an excellent game giving homage to the JRPGs of the 16 bit era. Pros 1) THE CHARACTERS- Once again, he fills his world with dynamic and interesting characters. The writing for each is nearly perfect in consistancy regarding their personalities and quirks. Some writers can be pretty jarring when people do a 180 with personalities in JRPGs, but here characters are written well, and actually develop and change over time through trials and hardships. This isnt an "everyone just worships you for no reason" game like so many these days....No, here you need to earn respect despite being the son of a famous couple (from the first game). Speaking of, most of the characters from the original are here in some form or another, much older and wiser (except maybe Ark....Never change man....Never change) Theres plenty to like here even if you didnt play the first game. But I HIGHLY recommend you get it and play it, because you'll get much more out of this one if you do. 2) A not so linear story Like the original, choices, actions, and words matter more than you might think. Things that didnt seem important may end up shaping whole paths. There is a ton of replay value here because of the different choices, routes, ect. And the consequences can me mild to life altering for said choices. But the thing is, there IS no "wrong" way to do things. Play your way and just make through your first run, then replay and try doing things differently. I'm about halfway through, and so far this held true in the original AND here, as I did reset to see how much I could alter things..... 3) The dungeon is MUCH more rewarding, and far better balanced than the original. You will feel like your progressing, especially financially, alot sooner than the original, which could sometimes feel so grindy just to make a few 1000 gold (without using cheesy tricks with seeds ect) that you were like a hamster on a wheel. This seems to have been better addressed here. And a typical 20 to 30 floor dive this time is going to net you rewards enough that it feels worth it now. Giving you more incentive to dungeon dive and grind. 4) The classes. Its pretty much identical to the original games class system. Everyone has a designated role (Warrior, rogue, mage, ect) and you progress in sub classes of these roles (Paladin, Water mage, Necromancer, ect). Its an excellent system, so I am not complaining that its so much like before because if its not broken, don't fix it. You can even mix some skills back and forth between sub classes to really power up and custom build your teams. Tons of characters to recruit, and I THINK its like the first game where as long as you don't reach a certain floor (because your in a race to the bottom with other dungeon explorers again) you can take your time, try different builds, and grind up....Not sure but it seems to be the case, and I hope it is. Deadlines in any game are lame. People want to play at their own pace in an rpg. 5) The town Its always changing, like the first game. Again you can build a home and decorate it with furniture (Some of which can be very beneficial and useful) and get ideas from towns folk to build facilities. Its a really cool way to take a breather from dungeon runs. Jobs are back as well, and more of them. They seem more flexible now, so that you can actually make some decent coin early on, and use them for the other benefits like better gear working at the blacksmith, or stat boosts working as a guard ect later. THE CONS 1) I can't hold the developer accountable for this, as they seem really nice talking to them in forum....But there IS a bit of "woke" sprinkled here and there. This is cringy stuff for anyone who was around before they used psychological brainwashing to hammer this into the minds of youths....Its not overwhelming and it doesnt really take away from the experience too much, but its there and I know this can push some people away. I hold this against their teachers/college professors and MSM really. If I had the time, I would take every person ages 18-26 to one side and have a LONG talk with them about who put that crap in their heads, and why. So just know going in that its going to be sprinkled around here and there. 2) The music Some tracks from the original, and some new tracks. But sadly, its pretty generic. Nothing "sticks in your head" like games of this style sometimes do (Of course its not fair comparing this game to games like Chrono Trigger or the Final Fantasy series in music, but they did such an incredible job with the rest of it, its a shame the music isnt up to the same level.) 3) SOME of the portraits/art There are new portraits and art that are just plain fantastic! Victors portrait looks 1000 times better than any of the protags portraits. This is because some of the original games portraits made it over to here, and they just arent up to the same standard as the new ones are. Not even close. Being honest, I HATED the original games portraits, but the splash art was fantastic. Here, the splash art and the new portraits are VERY well done, with the exception of the old style portraits, which just don't look like they belong in the same game. I hope this is a work in progress, and the new art will eventually do ALL portraits, because that artists work is a 9.5 to a 10! While the old portraits are more like a 5 or 6. Other than that, I really don't have any other stand out issues. The game is truly a labor of love and definately worth the asking price. And this developer is always improving their games. Hell, they kept improving the original for several years with devotion long after anyone would have felt they were obligated to. Thats a love of craft and devotion to fans you don't really see alot. The first game was such a good retro game that I bought this one the moment I saw it was available. And I wasnt dissapointed. And if you like retro JRPGs from the 16 bit era, you won't be either. Of that I am sure.

I don't get the game, can't seem to find any wind crystals to get out of the dungeon even after crawling through 3 full levels. It's a traditional rpgmaker-style game, where you go around doing minipuzzles to earn gold, buff up your party, and then head to the dungeon. The problem is, the dungeon is somehow ridiculously difficult. You need to find wind crystals to get out, and they are _not_ common at all, not on every level. If you die you lose all your items, I know that's supposed to be acceptable but it's just lame in my opinion. What I did on my second run, is to spend 60 minutes just running around doing the jobs, so I could get the best equipment for the equipment store for both of my characters (yes initially you could only have 2). You would think that would be enough to survive the dungeon, no. I followed the advice to clear out the whole floor before proceeding, and went through 3 full levels before I died. The issue is the monsters are pretty damn strong even at level 1, and they run as fast as you and they will chase you so you'll probably have to fight all you encounter. Perhaps I could do more work to buy more potions, perhaps the idea is to just keep on dying so you level up, and there probably is a whole game beyond that, but nah I play a dungeon crawler to crawl dungeons and level up, not to do repetitive work puzzles, and I have other games to play tbh, and it doesn't look like there's much beyond it for it to be worth the grind. Watch some gameplay videos before buying to see if you'll like it.

I recently played this game and was left feeling quite disappointed. The story line was lackluster and surprisingly brief, lacking the depth and engagement I was hoping for. The characters seemed flat and failed to evolve throughout the game. The combat was overly repetitive, which quickly became tedious real quick. Despite the potential for an interactive and choice-driven narrative, the game failed to deliver meaningful options, resulting in choices that felt inconsequential to the story line's progression.

The very first time I met her at the Backsmiths, where the blacksmith refused to take her weapon because it had blood on it, I knew it was the beginning of something special. But alas, The game prevents me from recruiting her or getting into a relationship with her. Anyhoo, if you like the idea of making relationships, doing activities around town and then going into the dungeon and seeing how the world reacts to the choices you make. It's the game for you. I rate the game No Mochi out of Mochi, the game prevents me from making very poor decisions and I don't like it. I CAN FIX HER! or the very least I can make it work. Would lament the fact that I cannot get Mochi to join again.

There's a half decent game here but it's buried under grind and bad writing. There's errors in basic sentence construction, grammar and even spelling at times and for a game where choosing the right dialogue option is critically important the vagueness of the writing is extremely irritating. If it weren't for the extremely detailed steam guide I could follow to pick the right dialogue options the game would be completely unplayable. Even worse than the writing is the grind. Want to start a quest? Get to a certain level in the dungeon. If it's with a party member? Take them into the dungeon a bunch of times. Advance their quest? A random level in the dungeon, sometimes you're told which one, sometimes you just have to check every level. Even worse are the fetch quests. Find 30 rocks or planks of wood or whatever, all only available on specific levels that you have to grind you're way to one level at a time. The worst one I ran into didn't even involve the dungeon, it was to collect 10 red fish. Each fish can only be collected by fishing and theres only a 25% chance at best so it took a solid hour of doing nothing but the infuriatingly slow fishing minigame to collect 10. On top of the grind there's plenty of RNG to make the grind even worse. with some events being randomly triggered and some floors only appearing randomly and even some that are a combination of the two! i essentially gave up on 90% of the quests and rushed the ending by following the steam guide and even doing that it still took 40 hours to finish. Probably 90% of that time was in the dungeon. My reward for all this was like two lines of dialogue and a recap of mostly characters I didn't care about. If you love RPG maker combat to the point of madness and don't care that most of the dialogue and story is poorly written and doesn't make sense then I can recommend this, for everyone else I'd give it a pass.

It's a fun little RPGMaker style game with easy, chill game-play and a story interesting enough for the type of game it is. It kills itself, however, like many small indie devs do to their poor games - it has quicktime events. This is a turn-based game that suddenly has you speed-racing a goblin on level 35 in order to keep going, and it's pass or fail. That's it. I *hate* it when these flash/quicktime style "mini games" ruin something. This could have been a fun little story but the unnecessary quicktime events where reflexes are tested feel really out of place in a turn-based romance dungeon crawler. They add nothing to the game. (There are other reviews I've seen mentioning the same thing about this game, so I'm not the only one it annoys.) I mean... include the little racing goblin or the mashing of buttons for people who want that kind of thing but leave chill, turn based games what they are meant to be - chill little turn based games. If it weren't for the quicktime events in this game that just caused me to stop playing at level 35 I'd give it a thumbs up. But as is? Yet another game ruined because a developer thought the audience for a harem/romance dungeon crawl style game was... timed speed events. Was there any player who thought, "Damn, racing that goblin really MADE this game!" - probably not. Were there players that just laughed and gave up on level 35 because of that? Most definitely. Sad, too, because if you could avoid all those events I'd be interested in the DLC.

This is a hard one to rate, I put a lot of time into this, trying to find every little secret I could, explore all the side quests and build everything I could find but all in all I think the experience isn't really worth the time investment. Lets start with the good, it's very long, there's a lot of content in here, plenty of companions, a lot of different ways to build, tons of equipment, plenty of side quests and story beats but beyond that it all feels like it has plenty of substance but no spice. The characters all feel very one note, a lot of them are weirdly aggressive out of nowhere, for instance, I tried to confide in the dragon blacksmith lady while listening to her story and she aggressively snaps back at me for interrupting her despite her having just ended her statement, it just feels so weird and instantly takes me out of wanting to help them. Besides the flat characters a lot of them are so weirdly sexualised, now I don't mind a bit of perv, that's all well and good but it feels like every 2 or 3 interactions someone would be ogling a girl or talking about a relationship or something along those lines, and I could forgive that but it's so constant over such a long time span. The worst for me is the psychotic murder girl that... everyone just lets roam around the town because she's in league with the rich lady? Like there's even an occassion where she straight up murders someone in the amazon camp and gets arrested and 2 seconds later she's out on the street again as if nothing happened, even after the ending nothing happens to her, she gets arrested then leaves, that's it. In spite of all of that you could probably have some fun with the character intreractions, some of them are sweet, and despite everything I do like that characters have their own sexuality preferences, some characters swing both ways, some are only into men or women and you can't get around that, I do however have an issue with everyone referring to me as a binary male or female despite allowing for gender neutral pronouns, it feels a bit hollow to have them if nobody particularly cares anyway. The actual meat of the game is making your way through a 60 floor dungeon, it's pretty tough and quite fun at first but eventually your player power will spike far ahead of the enemies and it becomes a slog, a lot of items or skills straight up break the game (weird fluid for instance is an item that's plentiful and basically kills any enemy in a few turns including the final boss) and eventually you'll find yourself just pacing through the dungeons over and over again to do minor quests or even just get back to where you were. The worst part for me was getting to the final floor then being told I need to come back the next day and just do it again. All in all there is fun to be had here, if I could I would give it a neutral review but steam doesn't allow that, pick it up on a sale if you can but it's a long investment

非常好玩的游戏！而且值得多周目游玩，因为你初始设定的职业决定了你可以参与哪个组织（魔法学院、盗贼工会、商人工会），每条路线能攻略的角色和剧情都是有差别的； 美术相比DD1全方位升级（宣传片就能看出来），唯一缺点就是部分角色艺术风格与大多数角色不一致，非常突兀； 能看到很多DD1的老角色作为彩蛋，很怀念； 游戏内容如名字所示：某个魔法都市发现了一个神秘的魔法地牢，实际控制这座城市的魔法学院执政发布消息：谁攻略了这个地牢，谁就可以成为第四个执政；故事便由此展开，冒险者蜂拥而入，你作为前代主角(ecallia地牢冠军)之子/女也来到这座魔法都市闯一闯； 常见的下地牢游戏，组建一支4人小队进行探索，队伍成员完全自定义，前期会有一点点roguelike元素（团灭的话会掉落所有装备脱离地牢，但是后面风之水晶多了之后基本可以带着战利品和金钱全身而退），战斗系统并不出彩，因为绝大多数boss吃各种buff，尤其是毒/灼烧；一些职业在我看来，很垃圾 但是出彩点完全掩盖了战斗方面的不足：首先可建立浪漫关系的角色众多（比第一部多很多），而且除了极少部分角色，大部分角色在你结婚前并不会放弃与你的恋爱关系（你可以体验很多浪漫），不同角色之间在下地牢时的对话，建设城镇，一些任务剧情等等都很有趣； 竞争对手方面，第二部的Quinn给我的厌恶感远远不如第一部的竞争对手Grant，Quinn感觉就是一个富有的、自私自利的、傲娇的婊子而已（你甚至可以攻略她），而且在与你的竞争中总是吃瘪，攻击性原因不如第一部的Grant，Grant是个真正的混蛋，一个真正意义上的自大狂，而且第一部中Grant会抓住一切机会嘲讽你这个冒险公会新人； 两个DLC：一个是纯支持性质的（开局给你一些道具和一个纪念章）；另一个则是一个很有内容的新任务，同时丰富了世界观 吐槽点：很多女性恋爱对象都是精灵，岁数按人类标准都很大（100+甚至更大）；人类女性恋爱对象呢，岁数也偏大，好像很少见到低于30岁的，哈哈；甚至还有带孩子的，很刺激了属于是； 而你，设定中只是一个20岁不到的年轻人类 同时很期待与第二部同一时间线的第三部dungeon dreams：wanderers了 PS：封面的帅哥不是主角。。。主角没有立绘，一个搓比，哈哈 与第一部剧情最后出现的的大反转不同的是，第二部的并没有那么大的震撼了，只是解释了下要举办这个这个竞赛的深层原因

party-based, turn-based JRPG with branching job classes, plenty of loot and interesting blend of dungeon delving plus social sim. Writing is good, art is nice, too. I'm enjoying the characters and their dialog so far. The dungeon delving is satisfying - I don't play enough games today that have you going far with limited and dwindling resources, putting the responsibility on you to know when to turn around versus risk going further - and that's a really strong concept for dungeon-delving. The game also does nothing to stop me from patiently grinding - which is exactly what I want to to. Love it. I'm not far in yet, but I enjoy this. For downsides/gripes so far - my controller works, but Im not finding it intuitive to make the d-pad work for this game rather than just analog stick. If there's a way, I just didn't see it. Other than that, I would prefer greater customization of the player character Azure - but the selections you get already by selecting your parents and picking either sibling is not bad. I know there's only so much customization that can be done in a game relying on portraits and sprites, and frankly this game is doing a great job of it - Still, I'll always ask for more.
